Many animals you were not allowed to hunt. Fawns, you couldn't hunt. Deer, maybe once or twice a year there would be a period to hunt them. So the whole society knew about that. That's why I was the gamekeeper, in order to protect the animals and prevent hunting out of season.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the woods that you would go to, in which you were hunting, would you come up against any dangerous animals?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, wild boar. There were no other more dangerous animals than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other animals were there?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: There were no other dangerous animals except for the wild boar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke to us about the children to whom weapons had been given and who began to shoot at birds. I think that's what you said, isn't it? And we put that episode in the summer of '92, unless I'm wrong. Could you specify what kind of weapons the children received?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: When Muhamed Pezer brought the car with the weapons from Slimena, he distributed to his neighbours in Ahmici, to all of them, even children ten years old and up. Those children would tend to sheep and cattle, and they were carrying small automatic rifles. I saw them, and they fired at anything. I already said that they fired at everything that moved, even at birds, and that's why I couldn't move around the terrain any more that I was entrusted with guarding as a gamekeeper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you remind us what period that occurred in? About what period was that?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: What time of day, or the year? What do you mean? I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm just speaking about the month, or even the season, in any case, during a year.

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the question is still not clear to me. What could you hunt at that time? Is that what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question, Mr. Alilovic. In respect of those children, some of whom were ten years old, who had been given automatic weapons and who acted somewhat dangerously, which upset you because they were firing on the birds with those automatic weapons, what period was that? Could you remind me of that?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The arms were distributed to my neighbours in Ahmici at the start of June and onwards, and then in July in '92, I could see -- not only I could see, but everybody else would see children going to tend sheep, and that they would be shooting from automatic rifles. This was in the month of June above the village of Ahmici. I have a forest there. I found three of them there, and all three of those children were carrying weapons and tending sheep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to yourself, who else saw that? The reason I'm asking that is because you're the first one who is telling us that, and I would like to know who else besides yourself saw those ten-year-old children using automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Nikola Alilovic, son of Ivo; Pero Alilovic, also the son of Ivo; because they also have forest up there, and they would go up there to cut wood. Then Ivo Calic, Ilija Jukic; they're all from Nadioci. They're all Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your brother Tomislav had come back from Germany on the 15th of April, 1993, and you told us that your brother Tomislav had been living in Germany for a long time, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 20 years. Where in Germany did he live?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. I don't know. We can call him on the phone if need be, and he can tell us, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What region did he live in?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the north, because he was all the way up in Germany, in the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What profession did he have in Germany at the time? At that time, what was his profession in Germany?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: My brother Tomislav is a railway man. He works for the railways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he have family in Germany, or did he have a family in 1993 in Germany?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: My Tomislav has a family. He still has a family today. He has a wife and a son and a daughter. His son is married; he also works in Germany. His daughter is married; she works in Germany. His wife works in Germany, and my brother Tomislav works in Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, why did Tomislav come back on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Why did he come back? Tomislav came -- he wasn't expecting anything. He came, and within three days he was looking for somebody to take him back to Germany so that he wouldn't be there in such a conflict. He didn't know that this would happen. If he had known, he would not have come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you to tell us why he came back from Germany all the way to Ahmici on the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Tomislav came to his house in order to see what was happening at home. The house was empty, and the house -- I look after it, I watch it. He comes on several occasions. He's at home right now. He comes to see what's going on with his house because everything he has is in that house. He just works there, but everything he has is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any reason to be worried about what would happen to his house?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, he did have a reason, because in that period, in the front and in the back, there was a lot of theft. There were many break-ins into houses, and things were taken from houses, and that's the main reason why he came back, to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When had he come back before that trip of April 1993? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: He comes every third month. My Tomislav has been on sick leave for awhile. He doesn't have to work there. He's there for a month or two, and then for 10 or 15 days, he comes home, and then he goes back. He goes back and forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he was coming?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew he was coming. We talk on the phone all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he come back from Germany?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: He came by bus, the bus that goes from Germany to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean he came in a bus from Germany all the way to Vitez; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: There is a bus from Vitez which goes to Germany, and it returns from Germany to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go back to something that you said about the young boy who had come to your house. I'm not going to say his name; we know his name. I would like to go back to what he said to you, according to your testimony. If I understood what you said, this young boy told you, "My father left the house taking the key with him and so you couldn't open the entrance door anymore, and that's why I had to go out of the house through the balcony." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will repeat it. That boy told me that they came out through the balcony, him, his brother, his mother, and his sister because the father had gone to the mosque for a meeting at midnight, and he had locked them from the outside, put the key in his pocket, and took it with them. So they didn't have a spare key. That's what the boy told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the boy explain to you how the soldier had gone into the house?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. Because they didn't break the door down, they had come through the balcony. If they came out through the balcony, that must mean that they didn't break down the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the young boy explain to you why the soldiers took him out of the house?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea. I don't know why. They told him to come out, that if they couldn't come out through the door, to come out through the balcony. Maybe the balcony wasn't high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the young boy tell you under what circumstances his brother had been killed?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He didn't say under what circumstances. Only when he had come out through the balcony, they told him to move away 20 metres, and then they shot him. I think that's what the boy told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what he said?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: We talked a lot. He told me a lot about other things too. But if I have a right to say it and if anybody is interested in that, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, if these are facts which will be of interest to the Trial Chamber and to the trial, I would be very interested in hearing them.

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: It's not of interest to me, but if it's of interest to you and if I have a right and if you permit me, I will tell you. I could tell you a couple of -- talk to you for two hours, if you're interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alilovic, when the young boy told you everything that had happened and everything that he saw, did he name soldiers that he may have recognised? Do you remember things like that?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't name anyone nor did he recognise anyone. If you permit me, he only told me, that boy, that his father, in the second conflict, was not to blame for anything, but in the first one, he was to blame, so he got walloped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you make that a bit clearer, please? Would you make that a bit clearer, please, Mr. Alilovic?

utterances.speaker: JOZO ALILOVIC
utterances.text: This is what the boy told me: His father, Babo, was not to blame for the conflict of this morning. He was not to blame at all. But in the first conflict, his Babo was to blame, but he got walloped on his back, on his ass. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I still have a few questions. Perhaps we could ask them tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 1.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of March, 1999, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
